objects.original: The actual finite-dimensional standard Gaussian on E, the fixed one-dimensional N(0,1), literal polynomial evaluation phi(z)=p.eval z, actual inner-product ridges for unit w, their genuine L2 classes and b=the scalar Gaussian L2 norm+1.
objects.reconstructed: The independent source-blind text identifies those same actual Gaussian laws and functions, MemLp2 witnesses hbase/hfeature, their indicated toLp classes, exact norm equality and the norm-defined positive b.
objects.evidence: The complete current module uses actual ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E and gaussianReal0 1, literal Polynomial.eval and the real inner product. No alternative function, covariance surrogate or arbitrary measure replaces them. The three approved blind definition-context entries describe exactly these definitions and genuine almost-everywhere L2 classes.

domains.original: Any finite-dimensional real inner-product normed E equipped with Borel measurable structure; every real polynomial; weights in the literal norm-one subtype. Neither positive dimension, nonzero polynomial nor evenness is required.
domains.reconstructed: Exactly the displayed NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace structures, arbitrary p:Polynomial R, and U={w:E|norm w=1}; base classes under gamma1 and ridge classes under gammaE.
domains.evidence: All binders are explicit in the sole theorem; no variable or section declarations or hidden domain restriction occur. Finite dimensionality over R entails needed completeness. If dim E=0, U is empty but scalar membership and b>0 still hold. Zero or odd polynomials are allowed. The claim is not extended to nonunit vectors or arbitrary rotation-invariant laws.

quantifiers.original: For every E and p produce scalar L2 membership and its fixed positive b, then produce membership for every unit direction and the same exact norm and common bound.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For all E,p, existential hbase; then define b from that fixed witness; assert b>0 and existentially choose a single family hfeature for every w:U; for every w assert norm equality and bound using that same family and base norm.
quantifiers.evidence: The existential proof witnesses do not choose different functions: hbase concerns fixed phi and hfeature w concerns fixed x↦phi(<w,x>). Proof irrelevance and toLp of a fixed function/measure prevent changing the norm by choosing membership proofs. The base and b precede the universal direction quantifier. No assumed unit-vector existence is needed for the zero-dimensional case.

assumptions.original: Only the stated finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel structure, real polynomial and exact unit restriction with actual Gaussian laws. No scalar moment, feature moment, covariance or bound premise.
assumptions.reconstructed: Only those structural inputs and p are supplied. Both base/feature MemLp membership, strict positivity, exact norm transport and uniform bound are outputs, not hypotheses.
assumptions.evidence: Step1 and actual proof hpow use finite moments of the real Gaussian at exponent2n, convert |z^n|²=|z|^(2n), and use polynomial addition/monomial scaling induction to construct hbase. Step2 hmap derives the exact unit-projection pushforward from Gaussianity, actual mean0, variance equal to the squared dual norm, and norm w=1. Mere covariance equality for a non-Gaussian law would not suffice; the actual Gaussian premise is used. No target-shaped moment/norm assumption or fake closure is present.

conclusion.original: phi is genuinely in L2(gamma1); b=||phi||+1 is positive; every actual unit ridge is in L2(gammaE), with norm exactly ||phi|| under gamma1 and hence at most b.
conclusion.reconstructed: The source-blind reconstruction recovers all these membership, positivity, exact equality and bound conclusions, including the fixed actual functions, measures and proof witnesses.
conclusion.evidence: Step3 constructs a measurable measure-preserving projection, obtains actual MemLp by comp_measurePreserving and exact norm equality by Lp.norm_compMeasurePreserving. Step4 obtains b>0 from norm nonnegativity and +1 and the common bound from that equality. The displayed source formula uses strict norm<b; this is also an immediate consequence of norm equality and b=base norm+1, although the theorem explicitly concludes the non-strict bound. No conclusion is lost. For p=0 both norms are0 and b=1.

scopes.original: One library-authored Gaussian polynomial ridge producer and four mathematical proof steps, placed by topic near Gaussian foundations. Integrated L2 control, without pointwise feature bounds, label moments, arbitrary-law averaging, global risk variation or process guarantees.
scopes.reconstructed: The same actual-law/unit-direction scope. The reconstruction does not add nonunit, non-Gaussian, parameter-law, particle or derivative conclusions. Empty unit domains are vacuous only for feature assertions, not base membership.
scopes.evidence: The actual current lesson and immutable authored source have identical mathematical statements, formulas, assumptions, all four steps, exact signatures/proof text and boundaries. Their sole JSON difference is current sources metadata adding the immutable citation to the previously empty list. The5-node/4-edge contribution graph covers the selected statement and four authored proof moves once each; it labels progression as source exposition, explicitly not elaborated Lean dependency. Excluded reader/Lean/navigation metadata carries no additional independent mathematical claim. No primary-book theorem, whole-model or stochastic convergence credit is inferred.

constant_dependencies.original: Exactly b=||p.eval||L2(gaussianReal0 1)+1, shared for all E and unit w; exact norm transport has multiplicative factor1. No direction/dimension factor or assumed existential bound.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same fixed scalar-law norm determines b, independent of E,w or proof-witness choice. The additive slack is exactly1, giving b≥1 and b>0, also when p=0. No coefficient or degree closed form is asserted.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The scalar base measure/function contain no E or w; hmap identifies every unit projection with precisely that law. The pullback isometry gives equality, not a dimension-sensitive inequality. The last proof step uses norm_nonneg and +1 only. A proof witness may be instantiated inside each E instance, but it cannot alter the actual scalar class/norm, so the mathematical bound is dimension independent.
